title: Build the project view's artifact totals, lint surface and located parse failures
statement: Add to `/`: artifact totals for each type, lint findings surfaced rather than re-judged, and reporting for a file that fails to parse — named with its path and a position, omitted from the page, and subtracted from its type's total. No rendered total may include an artifact the page did not render.
notes: ⚠️ Split from TSK-0007 on 2026-08-27, because the truthfulness rules are where this view fails SILENTLY and they deserve their own review rather than riding along with the navigation. ⚠️ THE COUNT RULE ADMITS NO PARTIAL-FAILURE EXCEPTION. AST-0035 measured the skeleton printing 178 while rendering 177: the total is what turns an incomplete page into a misleading one, because an operator reading it has been told the missing thing is present. ⚠️ ACC-0014 is evaluated against a FIXTURE of known composition, never against the page — the page renders totals rather than entries, so counting what it shows would compare a number with itself. ⚠️ DONE 2026-08-28. Nine tests: an offline fixture with a declared composition, a corrupt-one case, a control proving a file count and a parsed count genuinely differ, static checks that the panel re-judges nothing, and a production sequence that corrupts a file while serving, requires the total to fall by one and the located error to appear, then restores it and requires both to recover — with no rebuild and no restart. ⚠️ FALSIFIED WITH A CONSTANT TOTAL AND WITH SUPPRESSED ERROR OUTPUT, as required, and each failed only its own assertion. That separation is the point: a single check covering both would let a page that counts correctly but hides failures pass on the strength of its arithmetic. ⚠️ THE READER HAD THE SAME DEFECT THE SKELETON DID. `artifactCount` was `lint.records.length` — a FILE count — since TSK-0005. It was never displayed, so nothing had caught it; writing the component that would have displayed it is what did.
